[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"API Documentation with Swagger/OpenAPI in PHP"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial will guide you through documenting your PHP API using Swagger/OpenAPI. Swagger/OpenAPI is a powerful tool for designing, building, documenting, and consuming RESTful APIs."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PHP installed (version 7.2 or higher recommended)"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Composer installed (for dependency management)"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of RESTful APIs"},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Step 1: Install Swagger/OpenAPI Libraries"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"We'll use the 'zircote/swagger-php' library to generate Swagger/OpenAPI documentation from PHP annotations. Install it using Composer:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"composer require zircote/swagger-php"},{"order":10,"type":"heading","text":"Step 2: Annotate Your PHP Code"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add Swagger/OpenAPI annotations to your PHP code to describe your API endpoints, parameters, responses, and more. Here's an example:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":" $id, 'name' => 'Example User']; header('Content-Type: application/json'); echo json_encode($user); } "},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, we've used annotations to define the API's information (title, version, description) and a GET endpoint for retrieving a user by ID. The '@OA\Parameter' annotation describes the 'id' parameter, and the '@OA\Response' annotations define the possible responses (200 for success, 404 for not found)."},{"order":14,"type":"heading","text":"Step 3: Generate the Swagger/OpenAPI Specification"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the 'swagger' command-line tool (provided by 'zircote/swagger-php') to generate the Swagger/OpenAPI specification (usually in JSON or YAML format). You'll need to tell it where to find your annotated PHP files."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"./vendor/bin/swagger -o swagger.json ./path/to/your/php/files"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace './path/to/your/php/files' with the actual path to the directory containing your annotated PHP files. This command will generate a 'swagger.json' file containing the API specification."},{"order":18,"type":"heading","text":"Step 4: Visualize the API Documentation"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can use Swagger UI to visualize and interact with your API documentation. There are several ways to integrate Swagger UI into your project. A simple approach is to use the online Swagger Editor (editor.swagger.io) and import your 'swagger.json' file."},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, you can host Swagger UI yourself. Download the Swagger UI distribution and configure it to point to your 'swagger.json' file."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"// Example configuration for Swagger UI (using a simple HTML file) Swagger UI
"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"Step 5: Serving the Swagger UI"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can serve the Swagger UI files (including the HTML file and the 'swagger.json' file) using a simple PHP web server or a more robust web server like Apache or Nginx. Ensure that the 'swagger.json' file is accessible from the Swagger UI."},{"order":24,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following these steps, you can effectively document your PHP API using Swagger/OpenAPI, making it easier for developers to understand and integrate with your API. Remember to keep your documentation up-to-date as your API evolves."}]
